blocking_defects.criterion: dominant_action / modern pace (no shot over the policy limit; no relabeled repeated view)
blocking_defects.defect: From 40.0 s to 47.6 s the film holds one wide parking-lot composition: four small cars in a thin strip, with about 45 percent of the frame empty asphalt. The board declares s8-shot-2 as a 'close' limits-tag view from 43.61 s. The pixels show only a slight push-in at 43.6 to 43.8 s on the same composition, so the planned close is a relabel of the same view. From 41.4 s to 44.0 s the only change is the Weather limits tag swinging a few degrees. Effect: about 7.6 s of one wide view, where the 'tightened' idea is carried by the tag's printed word rather than a picture.

The clause 'swept into Salado Creek' is not performed legibly. The car is already sitting level in a flat, calm-looking brown sheet of water at 12.4 s. It barely moves from 13.0 to 14.6 s. It gains only a slight nose-up tilt from 15.2 to 15.8 s and a slow leftward drift from 16.0 to 17.2 s. There are no visible current lines, no rising water and no sideways lift as the board describes. Rain is faint ticks. Effect: muted, this reads as a car standing or floating in a pond rather than being carried off by fast water. Velocity between samples is unresolved at 5 fps.

non_blocking_defects.defect: The car's state is out of order. The car glides in and is parked in the bay with its brake lamp lit by 1.4 s and stays parked at 2.0 to 2.2 s. The cab cut from 2.4 to 4.6 s then shows the wheel turning and the airport sign sliding out of the windshield, so the car is moving again. It is parked again at 4.8 s. The phone reads 'Ride requested / Finding a car' until 5.6 s, about 4 s after the car is already at the curb. The hail-then-arrive order reads backwards. Fix in the same batch.
The declared bridge, a car pin riding from the curb onto the map, is not visible. The map pins are plain round dots. The map content is very faint at phone size from 6.8 to 7.4 s.

The standing water is a flat grey-blue overlay shape with small ripple marks and no depth or spray. The caption box's right end partly covers the water's first appearance from 30.0 to 30.4 s. The turn still reads.

Two separate forearms in blue sleeves enter from the same right edge, one with the pen and one with the stamp. They are long rigid tubes with no hand articulation visible at phone size. The s5 stamp hand has the same look. Native finish inspection is required.

The record card first appears lying tilted on the roadway below the car. It then grows over the road and overlaps the wheels, with no support or shadow. At 53.0 s it becomes a desk panel in a hard-seamed split. The phone prop also moves around: a screen overlay at 47.8 s, propped on the bench at 50.0 s, on the desk at 53.0 s.

Several shots leave the lower 40 to 50 percent of the frame empty (asphalt, paving, verge or desk): s1, s4, s6, s8 and s9. The subjects sit in a narrow middle band, which limits occupancy at phone size.

subject_recognition.observed: The white roof-pod car is recognizable in every car scene: curb, cab, creek, flooded street, lane, lot and curb again. The record cards are legible: Software, 3,791, Nearly 3,800 vehicles, the remedy sentence and both stamps. The s8 cars are recognizable but small, in a thin strip.

contact_and_consequence.observed: The creek current shows no visible action on the car: the water is flat and the car stays level, with only a slow drift and slight tilt. Elsewhere contact reads. The stamp touches and leaves its imprint at 26.0 to 26.8 s and 38.0 to 39.0 s, the check badges land from 44.0 to 44.8 s, and the door opens from 48.0 to 48.8 s. Secondary: the s1 order inversion from 1.4 to 5.6 s.

surface_finish.observed: The creek water is a flat calm sheet and the lane standing water is a flat tinted overlay. The forearms are rigid tubes. The car body is finished, with rims, empty seats, a mud line and lamps. Native inspection is still required.

closing_payoff.observed: The film returns to the same airport curb. The car's rear door opens, then the frame splits: the open-door car above, and below a card reading 'The remedy is currently under development' with its stamp and an underline drawn from 53.2 to 53.8 s. It holds to 56.0 s and answers the opening question without inventing an outcome.

story_review.one_viewing_summary: A driverless white car arrives at a San Antonio airport curb. A map shows where service began. Two empty cars sit in floodwater, in a creek and on a street. A federal record counts nearly 3,800 cars. A car slows, then rolls into standing water as the recall's 'may' lights up. The remedy is stamped under development. Cars take an interim update by April 20. The film closes on the open airport ride beside the unfinished remedy.
story_review.opening_to_ending: The opening question, what the federal record says about the flood problem, is answered by the closing split: the ride is open and the remedy is under development. No outcome is invented.
story_review.weakest_transition: s1 to s2 at 6.6 to 6.8 s: from the curb to a faint map table with no carried subject. The declared car pin is not visible.

strongest_frame.observed: Close side view of the empty car in standing water with a wake at the front tire, under the recall sentence with 'may' highlighted.

weakest_frame.observed: A thin strip of four tiny parked cars, about 45 percent empty asphalt, and only a tag swinging on a wire, mid-hold of a 7.6 s single composition.

notes: Muted image review only; sound not judged. Region (Bexar, blackland-san-antonio) is consistent: airport skyline, limestone creek ledges, single-story residential street. No retired motifs. Credits from 56.0 to 61.0 s use the current Lone Star flag only. Onscreen numerals 3,791 and 3,800 trace to the c6 and c13 quotes, and 60 traces to c2. Recommended consolidated repair: (1) give s8 a real close framing or an action cut so no view exceeds the policy limit, and fill the frame; (2) make the s3 current visibly carry the car (flow lines, rising water, sideways drift and tilt), not a level car in still water; (3) in the same batch, fix the s1 state order (phone request before arrival, cab interior while moving before the parked exterior) and ground the s9 card.
